summary: Locked file-write wrapper (cdecl, takes a file slot, buffer and byte count). When the slot is in range (a1 < uNumber) and the slot's descriptor flag bit 0 is set (descriptor array dword_8D4920, slot selected by a1 >> 5 and 36 * (a1 & 0x1F) + 4), it enters a critical section, delegates the actual write to sub_58E290(a1, lpBuffer, nNumberOfBytesToWrite), leaves the critical section and returns that result. Otherwise it writes error code 9 and error offset 0 through two TLS getters and returns -1.

local_names.a1: file slot index; selects the descriptor row and guards the write
local_names.lpBuffer: data source forwarded unchanged to sub_58E290
local_names.nNumberOfBytesToWrite: byte count forwarded unchanged to sub_58E290
local_names.v3: return value of sub_58E290, propagated on the success path

operations.description: Success path requires a1 < uNumber AND the byte at dword_8D4920[a1 >> 5] + 36 * (a1 & 0x1F) + 4 to have bit 0 set.
Enter the file critical section via CriticalSectionEnterWithLazyInit(a1).
Delegate the write: v3 = sub_58E290(a1, lpBuffer, nNumberOfBytesToWrite).
Leave the file critical section via FileCriticalSectionLeave(a1).
Return v3, the result of the delegated write, on the success path.
Error path: store error code 9 through the TLS getter at 0058afcf.
Error path: store error offset 0 through the second TLS getter at 0058afd8.
Return -1 on the error path (invalid slot or flag cleared).
Called by sub_5886A7 (005886a7), BufferFlushWrite (0058a05a), sub_58CF35 (0058cf35) and sub_59C1E7 (0059c1e7) as the serialized write entry point.

unresolved: The layout of the descriptor rows indexed by dword_8D4920 (36 bytes per slot, flag byte at +4) is not documented in this packet; the 36-byte stride and +4 flag position are taken directly from the raw source arithmetic.
Semantics of TLS error code 9 and of the two TLS getters are caller-visible state, not explained here.
The prelabel notes this is a structural twin of sub_58C331 (0058c331); that relationship is not independently verified in this packet.
